ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The mother of your husband or wife is your (1 mark)
   A. sister-in-law
   B. mother-in-law
   C. ancestor
   D. care-giver

2. Which word begins with the blend tw? (1 mark)
   A. tender
   B. tenth
   C. tennis
   D. twenty

3. Which comes first in a dictionary? (1 mark)
   A. market
   B. mother
   C. mat
   D. mango

4. Articles: Which is correct? (1 mark)
   A. A Kenya is beautiful.
   B. The Kenya is beautiful.
   C. Kenya is beautiful.
   D. An Kenya is beautiful.

5. Which article goes before 'hour'? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. no article always
   C. the
   D. an

6. Which word means a very big and special meal? (1 mark)
   A. feast
   B. ribbon
   C. snack
   D. chore

7. What is the plural of 'box'? (1 mark)
   A. boxies
   B. boxes
   C. boxs
   D. boxen

8. What is the plural of 'baby'? (1 mark)
   A. babyes
   B. baby
   C. babies
   D. babys

9. Which is a good way to make a story interesting? (1 mark)
   A. Copy a friend
   B. Leave out the ending
   C. Add small details and one simile
   D. Write very short words

10. What does 'proofread' mean? (1 mark)
   A. Read your work carefully and correct mistakes
   B. Copy from a book
   C. Write faster
   D. Draw pictures

11. Which is a minimal pair for /p/ and /b/? (1 mark)
   A. men, main
   B. wet, wait
   C. pig, big
   D. pen, pain

12. Which phrase do we use to get someone's attention politely? (1 mark)
   A. Move away
   B. Give me
   C. Hey you
   D. Excuse me

13. Why did the woman say Neema's mother had taught her good manners? (1 mark)
   A. Because Neema was late
   B. Because Neema was rich
   C. Because Neema was tall
   D. Because Neema spoke and acted politely

14. Language patterns: Which sentence is correct? (1 mark)
   A. We have chairs enough to sit on.
   B. We have enough chair to sit on.
   C. We have enough chairs to sit on.
   D. We have enough chairs for sit.

15. What should you use first when learning neat print script? (1 mark)
   A. A marker
   B. A brush
   C. A pencil
   D. A felt pen

16. Which word has a silent h at the start? (1 mark)
   A. hen
   B. hand
   C. hour
   D. house

17. Which pronoun replaces 'the children'? (1 mark)
   A. she
   B. it
   C. he
   D. they

18. 'She would like to be ___.' Which fits? (1 mark)
   A. to farm
   B. a farmer
   C. farming
   D. farmed

19. Listening and diet: Which word has the sound /æ/? (1 mark)
   A. juice
   B. fruit
   C. apple
   D. food

20. Which is an example of extensive reading? (1 mark)
   A. Learning a poem for an exam
   B. Writing a letter
   C. Reading one line for a test
   D. Reading many story books in your free time

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Describe how to find facts about a lion in a junior encyclopaedia. (4 marks)

22. Name three polite words or phrases and say when each is used. (3 marks)

23. Make a simple plan for a story called 'The Guests Who Came Late'. (4 marks)

24. Write a friendly letter of about five sentences to a friend in another school about new road safety words you learnt. (5 marks)

25. State two things you can find in a dictionary entry. (2 marks)

26. Write the subject and the object forms of: I, he, we, they. (2 marks)

27. Complete the simile and explain it: 'as cold as ______'. (2 marks)

28. Write three tall letters and three tail letters. (3 marks)

29. Explain how guide words help you find a word quickly. (3 marks)

30. Explain what the saying 'A stitch in time saves nine' teaches. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
ENGLISH LANGUAGE — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — mother-in-law
   The mother of your husband or wife is your mother-in-law.

2. D — twenty
   Twenty starts with t and w together.

3. D — mango
   Mango has n as the third letter, which comes before r, t and the o in mother.

4. C — Kenya is beautiful.
   We do not use the before most country names.

5. D — an
   The h is silent, so hour starts with a vowel sound.

6. A — feast
   A feast is a large special meal.

7. B — boxes
   Nouns ending in x add es.

8. C — babies
   A consonant comes before y, so change y to i and add es.

9. C — Add small details and one simile
   Details and similes help the reader picture the story.

10. A — Read your work carefully and correct mistakes
   Proofreading is checking spelling, punctuation and meaning.

11. C — pig, big
   Pig and big differ only in the first sound.

12. D — Excuse me
   Excuse me is polite.

13. D — Because Neema spoke and acted politely
   Her actions showed good manners.

14. C — We have enough chairs to sit on.
   The pattern is enough + noun + to + verb.

15. C — A pencil
   A pencil allows you to rub out mistakes.

16. C — hour
   Hour begins with a vowel sound, so the h is silent.

17. D — they
   They stands for more than one.

18. B — a farmer
   A noun phrase follows be.

19. C — apple
   Apple has /æ/.

20. D — Reading many story books in your free time
   Extensive reading means reading widely.

SECTION B
----
21. (4 marks)
   Answer: Choose the topic Lion, find the L volume or type it in the search box, use guide words or the index to find the page, read the text, pictures and captions and write short notes in your own words.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Please: when asking. Thank you: when someone helps. Sorry: when we make a mistake.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each phrase with its use.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Beginning: family prepares for a party. Middle: guests do not arrive, food gets cold. Problem: they lost the way. End: they arrive, everyone laughs and eats.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a beginning, 1 for events, 1 for a problem and 1 for an ending.

24. (5 marks)
   Answer: A letter with address and date, Dear ..., a body that mentions words such as roundabout, foot bridge and railway crossing, a closing and a name.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for address and date, 1 for greeting, 1 for body content, 1 for closing and name, 1 for punctuation.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Any two: spelling, meaning, part of speech, example sentence, pronunciation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (2 marks)
   Answer: I, me; he, him; we, us; they, them.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each pair.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: as cold as ice, because ice is very cold.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for a suitable comparison and 1 mark for the explanation.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tall: b, d, h (or f, k, l, t). Tail: g, p, y (or j, q).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each set, up to 3, with a mark for correctness.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Guide words show the first and last word on a page. If your word comes between them alphabetically, it is on that page. If not, turn forward or backward.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for what guide words show, 1 mark for comparing your word, 1 mark for turning pages.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: It teaches us to fix a small problem early, before it becomes a big problem.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for fixing early and 1 mark for avoiding a bigger problem.
